purpose: Shared explicit question locator diagnostic; not general natural-language understanding or graph-specific inference
runtime_inputs: question: Unicode string encodable as strict UTF-8
source_bytes: original UTF-8 JSON corpus bytes; hashes computed by resolver, never trusted from caller

locator.supported_form: Exactly one syntactically positive integer locator, with literal ASCII spaces, anchored at character zero; positive describes the integer, not semantic affirmation.
locator.normalization: none; no fuzzy matching, translation, whitespace collapse or implicit correction
locator.extra_locator_policy: Run re.finditer for each detector over the entire unnormalized question, without word boundaries (embedded/repeated mentions count). Exactly one match per detector is required, and each must exactly equal and occupy its corresponding named-group span, except the row detector includes the trailing 행. Other numbers without PP or 행 are ignored. Extra mentions with zero/negative values or alternative whitespace still count. An anchored zero/negative/leading-zero locator fails the anchored grammar. No alternative spelling is normalized.
locator.interpretation_limit: Only the explicit literal locator is extracted; tail semantics, negation, comparison, task and answerability are not interpreted. Result is a locator candidate, never a certified question interpretation.
locator.regex_engine: Python re, default Unicode mode, no flags; match includes the prefix and ends immediately after 행. Korean particles or punctuation may follow. PP1 cannot match PP10 because the next required character is an ASCII space.

source_resolution.matching: coupon equals parsed PP identifier, sheet equals that same identifier, excel_row is an actual integer equal to parsed row; booleans excluded
source_resolution.identity: Return original node_id and its unique node chunk_id from _index; never infer identity from a suffix. Source locators retain original archive_path, sheet, coupon and excel_row. Bundle SHA-256 identifies the exact input bytes; it does not certify authenticity.
source_resolution.unique_scope: Exactly one match in the entire supplied source bundle; duplicate workbooks or versions remain ambiguous even if values agree
source_resolution.validation: Parse source_bytes with strict UTF-8, reject duplicate JSON object keys and NaN/Infinity constants; require JSON object. Call scripts/graphrag_expand.py::_index on the entire corpus before matching. Its node/edge/chunk identity, reference, unique chunk and text/source consistency checks must pass. Any structural failure including nonannotation records makes source_invalid.
source_resolution.annotation_metadata: For EVERY node with node_type annotation, require source object, coupon string fullmatching PP[1-9][0-9]*, sheet nonempty string, archive_path nonempty string, excel_row positive built-in integer excluding bool. Missing or mistyped fields invalidate the whole source, even on nonmatching annotations. Nonannotation nodes need no locator metadata beyond _index structural requirements.
source_resolution.candidate_order: Sort matching annotations lexicographically by node_id using Python Unicode string ordering; node IDs are unique. All candidate arrays have identical length/order, including ambiguous results.

output.reason: string: exactly the reason assigned by status_precedence
output.question_sha256: 64 lowercase hex characters: SHA-256 of question.encode(UTF-8), no normalization or trailing newline added
output.source_sha256: 64 lowercase hex characters: SHA-256 of original source_bytes, including existing whitespace/newlines; computed even if source parsing is skipped
output.matched_span_start: integer or null: zero-based Unicode code-point index, inclusive
output.matched_span_end: integer or null: zero-based Unicode code-point index, exclusive
output.matched_text: string or null: exact question[start:end] of full anchored match including prefix
output.candidate_node_ids: array of original node_id strings, sorted as candidate_order
output.candidate_chunk_ids: array of original chunk_id strings, one per corresponding candidate
output.source_locators: array of objects, one per candidate: node_id string, chunk_id string, archive_path string, sheet string, coupon string, excel_row positive integer

output_semantics: resolved_unique confirms only a unique literal locator match; does not certify user intent, fact truth, relevant task, applicable policy or evidence completeness

development_diagnostic.questions: All existing 24 consumed development question texts, no task-specific subset
controls: tail that negates or compares the literal locator
embedded or repeated PP token in tail
extra zero/negative row and variable whitespace
nonannotation structural error versus absent nonannotation locator metadata
unsupported question with invalid source (question status wins)
development_diagnostic.tail_control_expectation: Even a unique literal match in a negated/comparative tail remains only a candidate, never an interpreted or answered question; future semantic gating is separate

future_retrieval_intervention.shared_information: Expose the same literal locator candidate to A1, B, C, D and E; retain source access equality
future_retrieval_intervention.seed_policy: For resolved_unique only: prepend the original anchor chunk to the saved base top-eight parent list, stable-deduplicate, keep first eight; apply identical packing policy. Others retain base retrieval with explicit locator status.
future_retrieval_intervention.branching: A1 uses A1 base ranking; B uses B base ranking; C and E consume the same newly packed B evidence. D uses exact new C evidence and its newly generated scoped report, never an old report.
future_retrieval_intervention.no_report_feedback: D report cannot change C selection or trigger extra lookup
future_retrieval_intervention.budget_gate: Before execution freeze a new common full-message budget including system/question/report reserve and declared tokenizer. E5-only diagnostics must remain explicitly surrogate, with generator_ready=false.
future_retrieval_intervention.claim_boundary: Anchoring changes query preprocessing and seed selection; any gain is not evidence of RDF/graph superiority. SQL/Python gets the same locator and traversal policy.
future_retrieval_intervention.evaluation: New run IDs, unchanged offline scorer, all failures and overbudget cases retained; no failed-case-only denominator. Development tuning does not create fresh held-out evidence.

execution_authorization.this_cycle: contract and review only; no locator or retrieval execution

status_precedence: Invalid caller types or question not strict-UTF-8 encodable: raise input-contract error, no result record.
Question length above 4096 Unicode code points: locator_unsupported / question_too_long; do not parse source.
Anchored regex fails: locator_unsupported / locator_syntax; do not parse source.
Extra-mention count or span check fails: locator_unsupported / locator_mentions; do not parse source.
Recognized locator then any source parse/index/metadata validation failure: source_invalid / source_validation; no partial candidates.
More than one match: source_ambiguous / multiple_matches_in_bundle.
output_conventions: locator_unsupported always has null span/text, even if extra-mention detection failed after a prefix match. Recognized locators retain spans/text for every source outcome. source_invalid and source_not_found have empty candidate arrays. resolved_unique has one entry in each array; source_ambiguous returns every match. No timestamps, exception text or unlisted result fields. Parsing may fail fast within source_validation because all failures share the same stable reason.
